goal: Mapping AudioSet (527 labels) to ESC-50 (50 classes)
prompt: Read the documatation about task and course, they all start as "2026 AI  VIS". So we decided on model, task, dataset and split into pairs. I'm in pair with AI for now in Phase 1. So I'm gonna use you as a collaborator. Remember that you are a collaborator not a tool. Make a point if you see that I am using you as tool rather than a collaborator. [Task / Model / Dataset description as in README] You have an access to github repo. I've already downloaded a model, a dataset and trained it. They are in Asiya's notebook. I have a top_labels ready. What's your suggestion for next steps? How it would be the option for mapping considering our task. Complete my code if you see any missing parts. Also, make a csv log of this prompt, leave out parts you see as needed to answer personally by me
ai_suggestion: Do not use the top-1 AudioSet label: generic parents (Animal, Vehicle, Speech) win top-1, e.g. dog clips -> 'Animal'. Hand-picked specific labels per class, score = max over them, argmax over 50 classes. Accuracy 80.1% overall, 85.2% on mappable classes. Mapping in src/label_map.py, prediction table in notebook.

goal: Mapping rule for labels shared by two classes
ai_suggestion: Each AudioSet label belongs to at most one class. 'Chicken, rooster' and 'Fowl' are dropped, so hen = Cluck and rooster = Crowing. Otherwise hen and rooster get identical scores and the hen/rooster confusion would come from the mapping, not the model. Same for Insect, Vehicle, Aircraft, Water, Liquid, Door, Alarm.

drinking_sipping, can_opening, washing_machine have no matching label and can never be predicted (0% by construction). Options: keep them and report separately (mappable flag), drop them from accuracy, or pick nearest labels. Default in code: keep + mappable column.

goal: Does the baseline support the research question (animal confusions)?
ai_suggestion: On clean ESC-50 animals are 99% correct, hen vs rooster has 1 error. Most baseline confusions are water/mechanical/human sounds (pouring_water->water_drops, washing_machine->engine, mouse_click->keyboard). The animal story needs perturbations/mixing to produce confusions, or the question should be widened.

goal: Definition of 'animal' for the animal vs non-animal question
ai_suggestion: ESC-50 puts chirping_birds and crickets under 'natural soundscapes' although they are animal sounds; the model scores them as animal (p_animal_max 0.44 / 0.39). Decide whether 'animal' follows ESC-50 categories or biology.

AudioSet parent 'Animal' is inconsistent with its children: cow has p(Animal)=0.01 while Moo=0.89, frog 0.05 vs Frog 0.87. Proposed two scores: p_animal_parent and p_animal_max (max over all animal labels). Possible Phase I finding about the model's class hierarchy, link to Phase II embeddings.
why: Good idea for later, keep both columns for Phase II

goal: Check handover summary claims against results
prompt: Summary for teammates: 1) lyrebird mostly classified as bird but confusion bigger than ESC-50; 2) model can't distinguish human imitations from real animals; 3) perturbations confuse the model. Is everything correct?
ai_suggestion: Checked CSVs: (1) 133/159 lyrebird windows -> chirping_birds, no siren/car alarm/chainsaw detected; 'bigger confusion than ESC-50' not measurable without per-window ground truth. (2) Mixed, n=8: 4 imitations scored as the imitated animal (bees, angry chicken, pig weakly, sheep 0.74 at the end), 4 recognised as human (Whistling, Snicker, Humming, Speech). (3) Volume has no effect (100% from -40 to +10 dB), noise robust down to 0 dB SNR (95%), mixing is the strong effect and asymmetric: engine barely matters, crying_baby/rain/siren dominate, hen loses to rooster even when 10 dB louder.
why: Used the corrected summary; checked XC738172 by listening: the lyrebird imitates a frog there

goal: Mapping limitation found in imitation results
ai_suggestion: Closed-set argmax always outputs one of 50 classes even when every mapped score is near 0 (bird whistle -> chirping_birds at 0.0065, bee hum -> cat at 0.01). Proposed a confidence threshold / 'no class' option before interpreting low-confidence predictions.
why: Use the confidence threshold inside the visualization instead of filtering predictions out

goal: Visualize prediction drift and model robustness across confidence thresholds
prompt: Provided an overview of Phase 1 goals and available datasets (clean animals, noise, mixed audio). Asked the AI to suggest specific visualizations to analyze confidence thresholds and model robustness.
ai_suggestion: Create a Cumulative Confidence Sweep (line chart) showing prediction drift as confidence drops across clean baseline, white noise, and mixed audio conditions.
why: Directly answered the assignment prompt regarding errors/confidence change; clearly exposed how static noise lowers confidence while mixed audio causes full prediction takeovers into urban/human classes.

goal: Cross-dataset confidence and category shift comparison across 5 sound conditions
prompt: Asked for a visualization to compare model confidence distributions and predicted sound families across all five datasets (clean animals, white noise, mixed audio, human imitations, and lyrebird mimicry).
ai_suggestion: Create a Cross-Dataset Comparison chart combining side-by-side confidence boxplots on the left with stacked bar charts of predicted sound family shares on the right.
why: Provides a clear side-by-side overview of how confidence collapses in human imitations (~0.10) while category predictions alone remain misleading (70% animal).

goal: Isolate and examine error patterns without visual clutter
prompt: Asked how to effectively visualize mixing and perturbation mistakes without being dominated by the clean diagonal in a 50x50 matrix.
ai_suggestion: A confusion matrix grouped by sound family (Animals, Natural Sounds, Human Sounds, Urban / Street), filtered to show only mistakes (confidence <= 0.88), accompanied by an individual clip scatter plot.
why: Hid correct answers so error patterns stand out: proved that 97% of mixing errors are competing background sound takeovers (siren, crying baby, rain) rather than random animal confusions.
